title: FASHION FOR RENT
subtitle: For questions 1–8, read the text and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
passage:
Fashion allows us to express our mood, personal interests, political leanings and so much more. The rise of fast fashion has made this [[0]] for self-expression more widely accessible, but it has also been an [[1]] disaster for the environment. We now buy twice as much clothing and keep it for half as long. Are there any viable alternatives?

Enter fashion rental websites, where you can borrow clothes for a fixed period of time. Might this innovation [[2]] a way forward for those of us who are [[3]] with fashion but also care about the planet? In theory, rental fashion could reduce the demand for manufacturing new clothing, which in [[4]] could reduce textile waste.

In practice, however, it [[5]] to be seen whether rental fashion is really as green as it's [[6]] up to be. Consider all the energy needed to deliver and clean the items. But, provided a greener infrastructure were possible, rental fashion might [[7]] be a good reason to [[8]] hope for a more sustainable future of fashion.

items.explainCorrect: **An unmitigated disaster** = a complete, total disaster — strong collocation.

explainIfChosen.0: **Unassailable** means impossible to attack or disprove — wrong before *disaster*.
explainIfChosen.1: **Insufferable** describes something unbearable — odd before *disaster for the environment*.
explainIfChosen.3: **Inculpatory** means implying guilt — wrong semantic field.

items.explainCorrect: **Chart a way forward** = map out or plan a path ahead.

explainIfChosen.0: **Survey a way forward** is not idiomatic.
explainIfChosen.2: **Log a way forward** is not a collocation.
explainIfChosen.3: **Cast a way forward** is not standard English.

items.explainCorrect: **Besotted with** = infatuated or obsessed with — fits *fashion*.

explainIfChosen.0: **Bequeathed with** is not used this way.
explainIfChosen.2: **Bewildered with** is not the fixed phrase (*bewildered by*).
explainIfChosen.3: **Besmirched with** means stained in reputation — wrong meaning.

items.explainCorrect: **In turn** = as a consequence; one thing leading to the next.

explainIfChosen.1: **In part** means partly — does not link cause and effect here.
explainIfChosen.2: **In excess** means too much — wrong collocation.
explainIfChosen.3: **In short** means to summarise — wrong connector.

items.explainCorrect: Fixed phrase **it remains to be seen** = we do not know yet.

explainIfChosen.0: **It waits to be seen** is not idiomatic.
explainIfChosen.1: **It happens to be seen** changes the meaning entirely.
explainIfChosen.2: **It stands to be seen** is not the set phrase.

items.explainCorrect: Idiom **not as green as it's cracked up to be** = not as good as claimed.

explainIfChosen.0: **Banged up to be** is not the idiom.
explainIfChosen.1: **Kicked up to be** is not the idiom.
explainIfChosen.3: **Whacked up to be** is not the idiom.

items.explainCorrect: **Nonetheless** = despite the doubts just raised, rental fashion might still…

explainIfChosen.0: **Furthermore** adds similar information — the tone shifts to a concession.
explainIfChosen.2: **Hence** draws a direct conclusion — too strong after *however*.
explainIfChosen.3: **Conversely** signals the opposite case — not quite the link needed.

items.explainCorrect: **Hold out hope** = maintain or offer reason for hope.

explainIfChosen.1: **Back up hope** is not a collocation.
explainIfChosen.2: **Put aside hope** means abandon hope — opposite meaning.
